Connie Health: $35 Million Credit Facility From Rivonia Road Capital Expandable To $100 Million For Medicare Brokerage Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:57 PM
Connie Health: $35 Million Credit Facility From Rivonia Road Capital Expandable To $100 Million For Medicare Brokerage Growth
Connie Health, a technology-enabled Medicare insurance brokerage, has secured a $35 million asset-backed revolving credit facility from Rivonia Road Capital, with the potential to expand the financing commitment to $100 million. The facility will support the Boston-based company’s national expansion through organic growth and acquisitions as it increases the reach of its AI-powered insurance distribution platform.
The financing is backed by Connie Health’s existing Medicare insurance book of business and is designed to provide scalable capital for expanding its network of licensed insurance agents.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the origination of new insurance policies and strategic acquisitions of businesses that complement its existing operations.
The arrangement represents an additional source of financing beyond the approximately $85 million in equity capital Connie has raised since its founding.
The company’s most recent equity financing was a Series B round completed in early 2025 and led by HealthQuest Capital, with participation from Khosla Ventures, aMoon, and Pitango.
Expanding A Technology-Enabled Medicare Brokerage
Founded in 2019 by Oded Eran, David Luna, and Michael Scopa, Connie Health operates an insurance brokerage focused on helping Medicare beneficiaries evaluate and enroll in appropriate coverage.
The company’s offerings include Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, and Medicare Prescription Drug Plans.
Connie combines a network of hundreds of local licensed insurance agents with a centralized technology platform designed to manage insurance distribution and customer service operations.
Under its operating model, customers are connected with a dedicated local agent who can help explain available coverage options, assist with enrollment, and provide support after a policy becomes effective.
The company believes maintaining these personal relationships can help beneficiaries navigate the complexity of Medicare coverage.
Its technology platform supports agents by automating and centralizing administrative activities.
These include lead generation, compliance management, back-office operations, and post-enrollment servicing.
By handling these functions through a common technology infrastructure, Connie aims to allow agents to spend more time assisting customers.
The platform incorporates AI capabilities intended to improve efficiency across insurance distribution and servicing.
The combination of local agent relationships and centralized technology is central to Connie’s growth strategy.
Using Asset-Backed Financing To Support Expansion
The $35 million facility provides Connie with access to revolving capital supported by its existing Medicare business.
Asset-backed revolving credit facilities allow eligible companies to borrow against specified assets or contractual cash flows, subject to applicable financing terms.
For insurance distribution businesses, existing policy portfolios and associated economic interests can provide a basis for structured lending arrangements.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the acquisition of new customers and expand its business through acquisitions.

articles.title: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
articles.snippet: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks SecurityWeek
articles.text:
Cloud Security
Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
Created by Zerto and Kashya veterans, the startup has launched a platform designed to recover whole cloud applications.
By
SecurityWeek News
|
November 11, 2026 (6:16 AM ET)
Flipboard
Reddit
Whatsapp
Whatsapp
Email
Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring back whole cloud applications instead of only the data behind them.
The round was led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Claltech also investing.
Dreeze , whose staff is split between Israel and the United States, said the money will go toward product development, bigger sales and marketing teams, and getting its platform into more enterprises.
The company was formed in 2025 by Avi Raichel and brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem. The three previously worked together at Zerto, which HPE acquired , and Kashya.
Dreeze’s argument is that getting data back after an incident is not the same as getting an application running again. A cyberattack or a mistake by an AI agent can leave an organization with its data intact but without the configurations, secrets, infrastructure and connections the application needs.
Its platform, named Application Revival, scans the customer’s cloud environment on an ongoing basis, works out which resources and dependencies belong to which application, and generates a recovery plan from the live environment. Backups of data and configurations are stored with those recovery plans in an immutable, isolated vault under the customer’s control.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
In a recovery scenario, Application Revival automatically reconstructs the application as a whole. Customers can also run recovery tests in an isolated account, with no impact on production.
“Companies have spent years getting better at backing up data, but getting the data back doesn’t mean the business is back,” said Ziv Kedem, the company’s CEO. “With cyber threats increasing and AI introducing new risks, enterprises need to assume that critical applications will go down.”
“We started Dreeze because recovery needs to go further. Our goal is to make Application Revival the new standard, so companies know they have a proven path to bring their applications back when something goes wrong,” he added.
The AWS version of the platform is generally available. Support for Microsoft Azure is in early access, with general availability expected in early 2027.

articles.text:
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 12:46 PM
Zus Health: $33 Million Series B To Expand Connected Healthcare And AI Platform
Zus Health has raised $33 million in Series B funding to expand its intelligent patient record platform, national healthcare data network, and artificial intelligence-powered clinical workflows. Drive Capital led the round, with participation from Sanofi Ventures, HealthX Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, F-Prime, Maverick Ventures, and JAZZ Venture Partners. The financing brings the company’s total capital raised to more than $100 million.
Founded in 2021, Zus is developing infrastructure that combines fragmented clinical information into a continuously updated patient record. Its technology is designed to give healthcare providers and applications access to more complete and actionable patient information without requiring each organization to build its own connectivity network.
The Zus Aggregated Profile creates a longitudinal patient record from information across electronic health record networks, pharmacies, laboratories, care-event notifications, and other clinical sources. An intelligence layer uses AI to organize that information and make it available through clinical and administrative workflows.
Zus supports pre-visit preparation, care transitions, risk adjustment, quality-gap closure, and population health management. Its Generated Patient Summaries transform fragmented records into concise information that clinicians and care teams can use during treatment.
The company’s national network supported more than 110 million transactions during August. Its AI-native clinical platform generated 39 million evidence citations during 2026 through the announcement date.
Zus also applied to become a Qualified Health Information Network under the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement. Its candidacy and HITRUST certification support its effort to participate in secure nationwide health information exchange.
The funding will be used to improve clinical intelligence, expand national data connectivity, increase record freshness, and support additional workflows across value-based and specialty care.
KEY QUOTES:
“The story of electronic medical records doesn’t end with the silos we have today. We’ve spent decades digitizing healthcare, but the information still doesn’t move with the patient. We’re building a networked medical record that changes that—connecting information across the healthcare system and making it available to the people and applications that need it. And now, with AI, we have an extraordinary opportunity to build workflows that actually make delivering care easier, faster, and more effective.”
Jonathan Bush, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Zus Health
“We believe healthcare is entering a new era in which AI can fundamentally change how care is delivered, but that transformation depends on having reliable, connected patient information. Zus has built the foundation to address that challenge at scale. Its combination of technology, market opportunity, and leadership gives us conviction in the company’s ability to help shape the next generation of healthcare.”
Molly Bonakdarpour, General Partner at Drive Capital

articles.text:
Anaergia: C$30 Million Credit Facility Expansion With National Bank Of Canada Increases Financing Capacity By 50%
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:47 PM
Anaergia: C$30 Million Credit Facility Expansion With National Bank Of Canada Increases Financing Capacity By 50%
Anaergia, a global technology company specializing in renewable natural gas and organic waste conversion, has expanded its revolving credit facility with National Bank of Canada by 50%, increasing its maximum borrowing capacity from C$20 million to C$30 million. The additional C$10 million in potential financing capacity will support the company’s working capital requirements as it executes its contracted project backlog and converts existing orders into revenue.
The amended agreement builds on the revolving credit facility originally announced on May 6, 2026.
The expansion provides Anaergia with additional financial flexibility to manage the expenditures associated with delivering renewable energy and waste management projects.
The amount available for borrowing at any particular time will remain subject to the facility’s borrowing base and other terms of the credit agreement.
Consequently, the increase in the maximum facility size does not necessarily mean that the entire C$30 million is immediately available for withdrawal.
Amounts borrowed under the facility may be used for general corporate purposes, subject to the agreement’s provisions.
Supporting Project Execution And Working Capital
Anaergia develops and delivers technologies that convert organic waste into valuable products, including renewable natural gas, fertilizer, and water.
Its business encompasses project design, equipment supply, construction, and operational services.
These projects can involve substantial engineering and equipment requirements, creating working capital needs throughout development and implementation.
The expanded credit facility is intended to support these requirements as Anaergia advances its contracted project portfolio.
Working capital is particularly important for businesses delivering large infrastructure and industrial technology projects because expenditures for materials, equipment, labor, and other activities may occur before customers make corresponding payments.
Revolving credit arrangements provide access to financing that can be drawn and repaid as needed, within the limitations of the applicable agreement.
By increasing its maximum borrowing capacity, Anaergia is seeking to improve its ability to manage project-related cash requirements.
Management identified the conversion of its contracted backlog into recognized revenue as a central operating priority.
The additional financing capacity is intended to support that objective while allowing the company to continue its focus on disciplined project execution.
Expanding Renewable Natural Gas And Waste Conversion Infrastructure
Anaergia provides integrated solutions designed to help municipalities, utilities, and industrial organizations manage organic waste more effectively.
Its technologies convert waste streams into renewable energy and other reusable products.
Renewable natural gas is commonly produced by processing biogas generated from the decomposition of organic materials.
After treatment and upgrading, the resulting gas can be used as an energy source in applications that would otherwise rely on conventional natural gas.
Anaergia also develops solutions that recover useful materials from waste processing operations.
